name: Characteristic-zero Yang Dimension
description: Yang dimension over a characteristic-zero field
definition: The **characteristic-zero Yang dimension** is $\mathrm{Y}_0(\mathcal H):=\operatorname{pd}_{\mathbb Q}(I^*_{\mathcal H})$, equivalently the regularity of the Yang complex over $\mathbb Q$. It has the same value over every characteristic-zero field. It is at most $\mathrm Y_p$ for every prime $p$. For a fixed finite class, $\mathrm Y_p=\mathrm Y_0$ outside the finite set of primes detected by torsion in the integral Hochster/interval complexes.
graph_summary: Yang dimension in characteristic zero. It lower-bounds every $\mathrm Y_p$; for a fixed finite class, only finitely many primes can differ from it.
origin_references: The underlying homological dimension was introduced by Yang in \cite{yang2018homological}; this characteristic-zero specialization is standard coefficient-field notation.

monotonic.proof: Yang's delta-versus-conjunction counterexample \cite{yang2018homological} has explicit cellular resolutions over an arbitrary field: on $2^d$ inputs the delta class has value $2^d-1$ and is contained in a conjunction class of value $d+1$. Thus monotonicity fails over characteristic zero when $d\geq3$.

doubly_monotonic.proof: Doubly monotonicity requires subfamily monotonicity, which is refuted by the recorded delta-versus-conjunction example.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Strict monotonicity requires doubly monotonicity, which fails.

p_monotonic.proof: At a fixed coefficient field, restricting the domain (projection) cannot increase the projective dimension of Yang's canonical ideal.
